## Brief

The likely cause: the Windows runner checks out text files with CRLF line endings (git's autocrlf on windows-latest), so `web/robots.txt` reads as `Allow: /\r\n`, and an assertion that matches a whole line (`/^Allow: \/$/m`, or a `split('\n')` then `===` comparison) fails against the trailing `\r`. Do not change web/robots.txt, scripts/build-web.js, or .gitattributes; if the real cause turns out to be something else (for example the built tree not carrying robots.txt on Windows), say so and fix the test or the build only as the cause requires, and explain.

Proof: `node --test test/build-web.test.js` passes locally; then simulate Windows by running the same test against a CRLF copy of the file (for example, run the test with a temporary `git config core.autocrlf` is not possible here, so instead prove the matching logic directly: a small node one-liner that applies the test's new matching to a `\r\n`-joined version of web/robots.txt's content and prints true). Quote both. `npm test` is not required beyond that file, but say so.
